test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Oct 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements about fundamental duties of the Indian Constitution is correct?

options.text: To preserve the biodiversity is a fundamental duty
To make compulsory education to children of 6 to 14 years as our fundamental duty
To obey parents is a fundamental duty
To save money for future is a fundamental duty

solution:
The correct answer is __**To make compulsory education to children of 6 to 14 years as our fundamental duty.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 51A deals with the Fundamental Duties of the citizen's states.
 
• The **86th CAA** added a fundamental duty which states that every citizen “**Who is a parent or guardian, to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years**”.
 
• These are **moral obligations to the citizens** of the country and are **non-justiciable.**
 
• Provisions as to fundamental duties cannot be **enforced by writs.** They can be promoted only by **constitutional methods.**
 
• Article 51a is confined to** citizens **unlike some of the articles related to fundamental rights which extend to **all persons.**
 
• So it is the duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for the education of his child.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 21A declares that the state shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This provision makes only elementary education a fundamental right and not higher or professional education.
 
• The right to education is subject to the limits of the economic capacity and development of the state.
 
• The government described this step as the dawn of the second revolution in the chapter on citizens' rights.
 
• To Obey the parents is not a **fundamental duty** of the citizens of India however it can be regarded as a **moral duty**.
